newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka buys bigger diesel lot with new terminal.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka buys bigger diesel lot with new terminal.

text.p: A new oil terminal at the port of Colombo has allowed Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) to import bigger shipments of diesel, a CPC official said on Friday.
He said the terminal, which was built in line with the port expansion, will be able to take 40,000-deadweight-ton oil tankers.
This will enable CPC to raise its monthly import of diesel and jet fuel per shipment to 250,000 barrels from its usual 200,000 barrels.

CPC has already started buying bigger parcels of diesel. In its latest tender which was for January 3-4 delivery, it bought 185,000 barrels of diesel and 40,000 barrels of jet fuel from Shell Singapore.
The usual size of diesel per shipment is 140,000-160,000 barrels, the official said.
CPC has also issued a new tender to buy the same volume of diesel and jet fuel for January 9-10 delivery, cost-and-freight Colombo.
This tender will close on December 18 with offers valid for two days.
CPC is buying more jet fuel and diesel for January arrival due to the scheduled shutdown of a 50,000-60,000-barrel-per-day for maintenance in mid-January.
